ApplicationId.description:
The application slug.

**Unique within one organization only.** It is never a global
identifier and never safe to use alone as a join or attribution key —
production has carried the same `application_id` for two different
organizations, and a guard that assumed otherwise crash-looped the
control plane. Join on the application UID.

Metadata.description:
Authored-only description and labels.

Absent from effective execution policy and from the policy digest — which is
what makes a cosmetic republish inert, and is load-bearing for `once`
execution: editing a description must not re-run a one-shot application.

Label.description:
A free-form organizational label. Authored-only: labels never reach
execution and never enter the effective policy.

Release.description: Where the application artifact comes from.

oneOf.description:
Liskov builds the artifact from the repository the organization's
source integration binds.

Spelled as an empty struct variant, not a unit variant, and that is
load-bearing: serde's `deny_unknown_fields` is silently inert on unit
variants of an internally tagged enum, so `{mode: source, builder: ...}`
would parse and drop the builder. An empty struct variant rejects it.
This exact artifact, by digest.

PinnedArtifact.description:
One exact, already-built artifact.

Carries only a digest. The CID, encryption mode and artifact kind are all
resolved server-side and recorded as evidence — authoring them would be
three more facts that can disagree with the artifact they describe.

Sha256Digest.description: A SHA-256 digest in `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` form.

oneOf.description:
The image is a generic catalogue environment; release selects the
application bytes. Catalogue/ABI compatibility needs resolved evidence.
LISKOV_WORKLOAD_DATA_DIR is supplied by the helper; authored variable
and secret destinations cannot override it in this arm.

JavascriptEngine.description:
The JavaScript engine. One member today; a union so adding one later is
additive rather than a re-typing.

file.description:
Relative to the **immutable artifact root**, not to the repository. The
artifact is what the processor receives; the repository is not.

ArtifactRelativePath.description:
A path inside the immutable artifact, relative to the artifact root.

Kept out of [`pattern_scalar`] because its schema pattern uses lookahead to
forbid a leading `/` and any `..` segment, and the `regex` crate
deliberately does not implement lookahead. The containment rule is therefore
checked structurally here while the schema keeps the ECMA pattern — so the
two are equivalent but not literally shared, which
`artifact_relative_path_agrees_with_its_schema_pattern` pins by testing both
against the same corpus.

Relative to the **artifact root**, never to the repository: the artifact is
what the processor receives.

RuntimeImage.description:
The curated environment a `native_image` application runs in.

Distinct from `release`, which is the application's own code. Pinning the
artifact does not pin the image, and vice versa.

catalog.description:
Which catalogue the image comes from. Validated server-side against
catalogue membership, failing closed on an unknown name — not against a
closed list in the schema (ADR-0057 §5, generalised 2026-08-12).

version.description:
A version **floor**, resolved to an exact digest at publication and
recorded in effective policy. Authors name a floor rather than a digest
so that a security rebuild of the same version is not frozen out.

ImageName.description:
A curated runtime-image catalogue or image name.

Deliberately a pattern rather than a closed enum. ADR-0057's 2026-08-12
amendment settles this for curated images: a versioned vocabulary whose
members are not knowable when the schema
freezes is validated **server-side against the published catalogue,
failing closed** on an unknown name. A closed enum would make every new
image a schema revision.

ImageVersion.description:
A curated-image version **floor**, resolved to an exact digest at
publication and recorded in the effective policy.

Authors name a floor rather than a digest deliberately (finding #2): a
raw digest is a mechanism choice where the platform has the better
answer, and it freezes out security rebuilds of the same version.

NativeEntrypoint.description:
An absolute executable and its argument vector, inside the image.

**No shell string is reparsed anywhere, and there is no inline program
body.** An inline body would be a second build and source channel that
bypasses the artifact's digest, provenance and immutability. Shell logic is
a file in the repository, built into the artifact, and invoked as
`/bin/sh /app/start.sh`.

AbsolutePath.description:
An absolute in-job path — a secret file destination, an image
entrypoint executable, or a state volume mount point.

The NUL exclusion is spelled `\x00` rather than the draft schema's
`\0`. The two are the same character class in ECMA regex, but `\0` is a
**backreference** to the `regex` crate, which rejects it outright — so
the draft's spelling cannot be the runtime check. Choosing the spelling
both engines read identically is what keeps this module's one-pattern-
two-consumers property intact; the alternative was two patterns that
could drift.

PayloadEntrypoint.description: Executed directly, without shell reparsing, relative to verified payload bytes.

Execution.description: How the author wants the application to run.

oneOf.description:
Run exactly one occurrence.

Reaching a terminal posture is the expected outcome, not a failure.
Running again requires an explicit, audited re-arm — a distinct "Run
again", never ADR-0050's "Retry now", which refills the pacing bucket
and means recovery.

An empty struct variant rather than a unit variant: `deny_unknown_fields`
does not reach unit variants of an internally tagged enum, and a
silently ignored `maxGenerations` on a one-shot is precisely the retired
knob this contract exists to reject.

Keep the application running; the platform decides placement, pacing and
path.

until.description:
Optional termination bound. Absent means unbounded — the only shape
V4 could express.

oneOf.description:
Start a fresh occurrence on a cadence.

Each occurrence has its own identity and terminal state; this is not
renewal of one long-lived job.

UtcInstant.description:
An absolute UTC instant, used as an execution termination bound.

Exactly one spelling: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. Offsets other than `Z` and
fractional seconds are rejected so that one instant has one authored form
and therefore one digest.

Calendar validity is checked, not just shape — `2026-02-30T00:00:00Z`
matches the pattern and is not a date.

Duration.description:
An authored duration: one integer and one unit.

Normalizes to exact milliseconds. There is no unitless form and no `mo`
unit — a calendar month is 28–31 days, so an authored spend rate over "1mo"
would mean different money in February than in July.

JobCount.description:
A count of Liskov jobs — total desired, per phase, or allocated to one
distribution value.

Schedule.description:
One paid job window.

`startDelayMs` and `maxStartDelayMs` are **absent**. The platform-owned
`standard` launch-timing profile resolves a 3 m schedule lead and a 3 m
processor start-within allowance, recorded per launch. Authors were setting
launch runway they had no way to reason about, and it is mechanism rather
than intent (finding #2).

duration.description: How long one paid job runs. Required on every authored schedule.

Phasing.description:
When the jobs in a deployment start relative to one another.

# This is the high-availability mechanism, not a load-spreading nicety

`evenly_spaced` with `jobsPerPhase` is how a quorum service survives
renewal. With three jobs and a six-hour window it staggers renewal by two
hours, so only one member is ever at its boundary; `simultaneous` retires
the whole cluster at the same instant, on a schedule.

The author expresses rolling replacement without naming a slot, an offset,
or a millisecond — which is worth stating out loud rather than leaving as an
inference from the words "evenly spaced".

oneOf.description: Every job starts and renews together.

Jobs are divided into equal phases spread across the window.

`jobsPerPhase` must be in `1..=jobs` **and divide `jobs` exactly**:
Liskov never rounds and never leaves a short final phase. That is a
cross-field rule, enforced in [`crate::v5::validation`].

Placement.description:
Where the application's jobs may run.

Commonly omitted entirely: open market plus mandatory platform-owned
processor intelligence is the default.

CapabilityMinimums.description:
Minimum processor capability, enforced **on chain** and fail-closed.

At least one key must be present: an empty block reads like a constraint and
is not one. Enforced in [`crate::v5::validation`] and published as
`minProperties`.

memory.description:
**Total device RAM**, not a budget this process is given.

The pool behind it is `v1_ram_total`. An author who reads this as "how
much memory my process gets" has misunderstood it in the direction that
causes OOM: it selects devices that *have* this much, and says nothing
about how much of it is free.

storage.description:
**Available** storage, not total.

The pool behind it is `v1_storage_avail`. The asymmetry with `memory` is
real and comes from the pools themselves, so it must not be smoothed
over in documentation.

ByteSize.description:
An authored byte quantity: one integer and one unit.

Binary (`KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB`, `TiB`) and decimal (`KB`, `MB`, `GB`, `TB`)
suffixes are both accepted and both mean exactly what they say. Unitless
numbers are rejected.

MetricScore.description:
A benchmark score floor for one capability pool.

Unlike memory and storage, a CPU score carries no unit, so the *name*
has to carry the semantics. It is also optional everywhere it appears:
a score is meaningless without a published fleet distribution, and most
workloads are memory- or storage-bound.

ProcessorSelection.description: A high-level processor source. Absent means the open market.

oneOf.description: An exact list of processors.

ProcessorId.description: A base58 Acurast processor account id.

Renewal.description:
How far ahead of a window's end the successor is planned.

Valid only for `continuous` execution — renewal must not define `once` or
`interval` cadence. Enforced in [`crate::v5::validation`].

oneOf.description: Liskov chooses the lead from observed launch behaviour. The default.
An exact lead the author is accountable for.

UpdateTiming.description: When a published policy version takes effect.

oneOf.description: Roll the change out as soon as it is published.
Wait for each job's natural renewal boundary.

ExistingJobs.description:
What happens to a predecessor job during replacement.

# One default, at one level

This block once stated its default **twice** — a field-level
`run_until_scheduled_end` and an object-level `stop_when_successor_ready` —
and they disagreed. Omitting the block gave overlap; writing
`existingJobs: {}` gave no overlap. Same authorial intent, opposite
behaviour, on the one setting where the difference is data loss rather than
a preference (finding #28).

The fix was to keep exactly one default and match the convention
`renewal.leadTime` already had. That convention is a required discriminator
plus a default for the *absent* block, which is why [`ExistingJobs::mode`]
has no `serde` default of its own: omit the block and get the default,
or write the block and say what you mean. `existingJobs: {}` is rejected
rather than resolved, because resolving it is what produced two answers.

# The residual risk is accepted, not overlooked

The failure modes are not symmetric: a wrong overlap default is
unrecoverable corruption for an exclusive-resource application, while a
wrong no-overlap default is a recoverable availability gap. Fail-safe
reasoning would favour the other value.

It was considered and rejected 2026-08-12 by the product owner, on three
grounds: it is what the object-level default already said, 46 of 47 drafts
omit the block and want overlap, and ADR-0050 is availability-first.
**No cross-field rule can close the gap** — the platform cannot detect the
exclusive-resource class, because `state.volumes` is not the signal:
`clickhouse` declares no `state` block at all, precisely because its data
lives in S3.

ExistingJobsMode.description:
The supported replacement outcomes.

Collapsed to outcomes deliberately. V4's `rollout_started` /
`processor_claimed` triggers exposed internal milestones and could sacrifice
availability; they remain effective-policy and read evidence only.

oneOf.description:
The predecessor serves out its paid window. No overlap, and a gap if the
successor is slow. Correct when two jobs must never address one
exclusive resource.

The predecessor stops once the successor is ready, so the two overlap.
The default, and what availability-first recovery wants.

Readiness.description: A probe from the same immutable payload, with its own bounded execution.

StateCompatibility.description: A declaration, never inferred database rollback or an execution guarantee.

perJob.description:
The cap on one delivered occurrence, including every failed attempt and
custody-specific register, environment, closeout, and deregistration
exposure linked to it.

The platform's fee reservation comes out of this amount and the rest
becomes the reward ceiling, so it is total exposure rather than a reward
budget with a fee bolted on. V4 called it
`maxServiceCreditMicrosPerGeneration`; renamed because authors should
not have to understand generations.

rate.description:
The lifetime ceiling, expressed as a rate.

Required when execution is recurring — enforced in
[`crate::v5::validation`], using the frozen
[`crate::ExecutionIntent::is_recurring`] predicate rather than a second
opinion about what recurring means.

ChainSpendUnit.description:
The denomination a cap is expressed in.

Discriminates *which custody path pays*, and therefore drives control-plane
behaviour rather than merely describing it. Thin V5 has one custody path:
ADR-0082 §3.a defers self-custody ACU spend, which needs a customer signer on
the live chain — an independent product program. The unit stays a named enum
rather than collapsing into the surrounding struct precisely because the
deferral is about *which wallet pays*, and a later version reintroducing that
question must reintroduce it here.

oneOf.description: Managed custody: Liskov's Service Credits pay.

Micros.description:
An exact integer amount of the smallest unit of account, as a decimal
string.

**Never a JSON number.** Money does not go through a float: an IEEE 754
double loses exactness above 2^53, and a spend cap that silently rounds is a
spend cap that does not hold. The denomination is carried separately by the
authored spend unit — Service Credit micros under managed custody, ACU
planck under self-custody.

window.description:
Defaults to `30d`, matching `billing::SpendGuards::budget_window_days`.

There is no `mo` unit: a calendar month is 28–31 days, so an authored
monthly rate would mean different money in February than in July.

Access.description: Operator access to a running job.

SshAccess.description: SSH access and who provides it.

oneOf.description:
Managed blind access (ADR-0045). Liskov brokers the session without
being able to read it.

Configuration.description: Variables and secrets for the job.

oneOf.description: A constant, part of the authored document and its digest.
A value the platform resolves out of policy at delivery time.

required.description: Whether the job may start without it. Absent means required.

default.description:
Fallback for the mutable value. Valid only here — on a literal it
would be a second value for one name.

EnvName.description:
An environment variable name.

Destinations must not collide: a name claimed by both
`configuration.variables` and a `configuration.secrets` destination is
rejected at authoring time rather than resolved by precedence.

required.description: Whether the job may start without it. Absent means required.

SecretId.description:
The customer-facing identifier of one declared secret.

`bundleId` is deliberately absent: it exposed Lockbox grouping
mechanics with no customer semantics, and is derived.

SecretDestination.description: Where a secret lands inside the job.

oneOf.description:
An environment variable. Collides with a variable of the same name, and
that collision is rejected at authoring time rather than resolved by
precedence.
A file. Never collides with an environment name.

Observability.description:
Managed logging.

ADR-0046. `logs.enabled` is the sole authored switch. `profileId`,
`sinkName` and `context` are removed: they exposed sink mechanics with no
customer semantics, and V4 already emitted deprecation diagnostics for all
three.

`runtimeDiagnostics.signed` is derived, not authored — `false` is invalid,
because signed diagnostics are a trust invariant rather than a preference,
and a control whose only valid value is a constant is not a control.

State.description: Durable-state intent. Required at the manifest root so opt-out is explicit.

oneOf.description: The application deliberately uses no Liskov state service.

holdOnFailure.description:
Hold a failed job instead of recovering it, so it can be inspected.

The honest spelling of what `maxRetries: 0` was being abused for
(ADR-0050). Naming the intent means the platform can treat it as a
diagnostic hold rather than as a retry budget of zero, which is what made
the old spelling a foot-gun: it silently disabled recovery for the
application's whole life.
